children: Wall Street's major market averages advanced as continued AI spending drove capital markets activity and sector rotation into technology.

A surge in AI-related capital expenditure by major firms is reshaping technology capital markets, driving record levels of capital-raising activity, according to a report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.
This is creating unprecedented demand for financing, while simultaneously driving sector rotation as investors seek exposure to the AI supply chain, the report noted, citing experts.
State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) advanced 3.52% week-over-week, while State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF
declined 1.83% amid renewed AI disruption fears.
Banks, insurers, and other related stocks that depend on consumer inertia
from the early popularity of Meta's Muse, an AI agent that executes multi-step tasks on a user's behalf.
Payment stocks slumped over disruption fears when a Muse checkout screen featured Meta Pay as an option, a report by Bloomberg showed.
Meta's Muse AI agent is reshaping sector rotation as risk appetite grows among investors, a separate Bloomberg report noted. On the other hand, XLF hit its lowest level since early July.
Among financial megacap stocks, Wells Fargo
led the decliners, shedding 3.66% from the prior week to close at $82.97.
The week saw the Wall Street giant
the retirement of its chief risk officer, Derek Flowers. COO Scott Powell was named a successor.
"Derek played a pivotal role in strengthening our risk and control framework and fostering the strong risk culture that positions Wells Fargo for continued growth," CEO Charlie Scharf had said.
Morgan Stanley
followed, with a 3.10% retreat to $196.31.
A Morgan Stanley employee is said to have

an internal document that had details on over 100 investment banking deals of the company in Asia and the EMEA region. The bank was working to contain the damage arising from the leak as regulators in India and China assessed the incident.
Citigroup
was the top advancer, adding 1.90% week-over-week to $134.28.

The week saw Citi sweetening the pot to lure new customers and persuade existing clients to bring more of their assets over to the bank by offering a higher savings rate under a new feature called Premium Boost.

Additionally, the company launched Citi Commerce Media, a platform that will use transaction-based data to help brands recognize emerging consumer needs, identify engagement opportunities, and measure campaigns' effectiveness.
Among largecap stocks, Pershing Square
(+12.90% W/W to $56.16) was a notable winner. The week saw Bill Ackman's closed-end fund listed on the London Stock Exchange, Pershing Square Holdings
, announce an up to $100M share repurchase program.
Ameriprise Financial
topped the losers. The stock lost 9.43% to close the week at $493.00 as the launch of Evergreen.ai, an AI-powered financial advice app, renewed AI disruption fears.
Allstate

followed with an 8.90% decrease to $227.60. Banks, insurers, and other related stocks that depend on consumer inertia had come under pressure from the early popularity of Meta's Muse, an AI agent that executes multi-step tasks on a user's behalf.
Lincoln International
(-10.49% W/W to $23.37) led the midcap decliners amid AI disruption fears.
Figure Technology Solutions
was the second largest loser, falling 10.12% from the previous week to $31.90. Bitcoin
was hit after an economic report indicated hotter-than-expected business activity.
Miami International

(-10.03% W/W to $34.90) was the next on the list. The company said on Thursday its full-service futures commission merchant, Dorman Trading, is now a clearing member of The Options Clearing Corporation.
Brighthouse Financial

(+6.59% W/W to $53.24) was a winner in the category after a report that Sixth Street is considering a renewed bid to buy the life insurer as a pending deal with Aquarian languished under regulatory review.
StablecoinX
, a stablecoin infrastructure company, was a notable smallcap gainer, adding 69.28% week-over-week to $17.25. Orion180 Insurance
(-17.92% W/W to $9.57) was a major loser.
